Face Landmarker calls are synchronous, so this implementation follows [Google's Web Worker recommendation](https://developers.google.com/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/face_landmarker/web_js).

The public camera engines render canvases, not a finished recording container. A host can capture snapshots or use a browser-supported `MediaRecorder` on the canvas stream, enforce its recording duration/size limits and offer an explicit download. Studio's host limits recording to 30 seconds/32 MiB. It requests no microphone track for this feature. These effects are not identity face swaps, emotion detection or a guarantee of frame-rate on every device. Stop all camera tracks when the workspace closes or becomes hidden, including late permission responses; `createCameraLease` handles that late-response ownership.

##### Landmark smoothing

Raw face and pose landmarks jitter by a pixel or two at rest, and a fixed low-pass that hides the jitter also lags behind a fast turn. `landmark-filter` implements the [One-Euro filter](https://gery.casiez.net/1euro/) (Casiez, Roussel and Vogel, CHI 2012): its cutoff rises with the signal's speed, so values hold still at rest and follow quick moves. It runs anywhere, including Node, and has no dependencies.

```js
import { createOneEuroFilter, createOneEuroVectorFilter } from '@optimai/creative-agents/landmark-filter';

const x = createOneEuroFilter({ minCutoff: 1, beta: .5 });
x.filter(rawX, performance.now()); // timestamps in ms; cutoffs in Hz

// 33 pose landmarks × (x, y, z): each landmark adapts to its own 3D speed.
const pose = createOneEuroVectorFilter(33 * 3, { minCutoff: .8, beta: 2, stride: 3 });
const smoothed = pose.filter(flatLandmarks, performance.now());
```

`minCutoff` sets stillness at rest (lower is steadier), `beta` sets how quickly the cutoff opens with speed (higher lags less) and `dCutoff` smooths the speed estimate. With `stride`, components are grouped into points that adapt to their Euclidean speed, so a diagonal move is filtered like a straight one and a moving hand does not unlock a still shoulder. The first sample passes through unchanged. A repeated or earlier timestamp, or a non-finite value, holds the previous output. `reset()` starts over, for example after the subject changes.

`createFaceRigSmoother()` in `camera-runtime` applies this to a `FaceRig`. Head rotation (yaw, pitch, roll) adapts to its combined angular speed; each expression coefficient adapts on its own, so a blink closes fully without unlocking the jaw. Tune with `{ pose, expression }` over the `FACE_RIG_FILTER` defaults. The output stays within the range of its inputs. `smoothFaceRig(current, target, elapsedMs)`, a fixed 80 ms moving average, remains available.

#### Local Ollama writing

Import `@optimai/creative-agents/agent-runtime` in a bundler or `./src/agent-runtime.mjs` directly. The runtime uses native fetch and accepts only a literal loopback HTTP Ollama endpoint (`127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`), defaulting to `http://127.0.0.1:11434`. It rejects remote URLs, DNS hostnames including `localhost`, credentials, query strings, redirects and cloud model identifiers. It first checks the installed model list and model metadata, then requests structured generation. It validates the returned document and allows one bounded repair attempt for malformed model output. There is no automatic model download, fallback to a paid remote provider or proprietary Studio dependency.

```js
import { getLocalModelStatus, runCreativeAgent } from './src/agent-runtime.mjs';

const controller = new AbortController();
const status = await getLocalModelStatus({ signal: controller.signal });
if (!status.available) throw new Error('Start your local Ollama service first.');
console.log(status.models.map((entry) => entry.name));

// Choose a name from the installed-model list, for example from your UI selector.
const model = modelSelect.value;
const document = await runCreativeAgent({
  templateId: 'story-seed',
  values: { form: 'manga', style: 'manga', audience: 'all ages' },
  brief: 'An explorer helps a lost cloud find its way home.',
  model,
  signal: controller.signal
});
console.log(document.title, document.summary, document.sections);
// AbortController cancels the inference request.
// document.studioPrompt can be reviewed before a separate Studio handoff.
```

The result contains a title, summary, sections with headings and body text, a reviewed Studio prompt, model name, provider and template ID. It is a written creative artifact rather than an image, animation or completed Studio project. Treat model output as plain untrusted text; do not evaluate it or render it as raw HTML. Run only one local model job at a time and let users stop it. Model size and hardware determine inference speed; the SDK does not promise a universal completion time.

Eligible installed models must support local completion and have a reported size of at most 8 GiB. Cloud and embedding-only models are excluded. The runtime checks eligibility before sending a generation request.

Storyboard Builder generates a purpose, action, visual treatment, framing, dialogue and sound direction for every scene. Prompt Branches generates a shared premise, complete prompt and explanation of the difference for every alternative. The model writes these as separate structured fields; the SDK validates them and formats their public body text as labeled lines. Explicit art direction must remain in every scene or prompt, and branches retain a supported paired-cast premise. Scene and direction numbers are supplied by the SDK. These structural checks help preserve the brief; users should still review the creative result before production.

The recipe's `network: "none"` and `execution: "declarative"` describe the **recipe's privileges**: it cannot supply code, choose remote endpoints or grant itself access. The trusted host may explicitly download the fixed browser model assets or perform validated loopback inference. A host that supplies a `baseUrl` must still use a validated local endpoint. `fetchImpl` exists for controlled tests and dependency injection, not to enable an untrusted recipe to choose its own transport.

#### Video export with WebCodecs

Install the optional reviewed peer in the host: `npm install --save-exact mediabunny@1.62.1`. The SDK never imports it; the host passes the module to `probeVideoExport({ mediabunny })` and `encodeCanvasVideo({ mediabunny })`, so a bundle without it still offers the MediaRecorder path. mediabunny is licensed under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (file-level copyleft), not MIT: using it unmodified as a dependency keeps your own code under your license, but changes to its files must be shared under MPL-2.0. The SDK does not vendor or redistribute it.

WebCodecs needs a secure context and `VideoEncoder`, `VideoFrame` and, for sound, `AudioEncoder`. Encoder support differs by browser and platform (some builds lack H.264 or AAC), which is why the probe tries several codecs and containers and always reports the recorder fallback. See [export video](docs/host-integration.md#export-video-with-webcodecs-or-the-recorder) for the host flow.

#### Run a standalone agent from the command line

Choose an eligible model already installed in your Ollama service. These commands perform real local inference and print the validated artifact as JSON. `--agent` and `--manifest` are mutually exclusive; `--model` is always explicit. A manifest supplies its own approved settings and creative brief, with optional additional direction from `--brief`.

```sh
npm run run -- --agent story-seed --model qwen3.5:2b --brief "An explorer helps a lost cloud find its way home."
npm run run -- --manifest agents/cloud-companion/agent.json --model qwen3.5:2b
```

For a local Ollama service on another port, the host can set `OPTIMAI_OLLAMA_URL`. The Node SDK honors this host setting when `baseUrl` is omitted; an explicit `baseUrl` takes precedence. The CLI and MCP adapter pass the same configuration through the literal-loopback validator. A browser does not read host environment variables, and an endpoint cannot be supplied by a recipe or point at a remote provider.

```sh
OPTIMAI_OLLAMA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11435 npm run run -- --agent style-brief --model qwen3.5:2b --brief "A warm, illustrated cloud adventure."
```

Use `node scripts/run.mjs ...` or `npm --silent run run -- ...` when a program needs only JSON on stdout, without npm's command banner. Errors are structured JSON on stderr. Ctrl+C cancels the inference request. The run command does not download a model or write a generated artifact unless you intentionally redirect its output.

The smoke command runs all five writing agents sequentially with public example text and their default settings. The runtime validates each artifact's structure, exact section count, required headings, bounded content and absence of repeated filler. The report includes each artifact and elapsed time. It stops with an error if an agent fails validation; it does not fabricate a successful result. `--report` writes only a specifically requested new JSON file and refuses to overwrite an existing file.

```sh
OPTIMAI_OLLAMA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11435 npm run smoke -- --model qwen3.5:2b --report /absolute/path/to/new-agent-smoke-report.json
```

`npm test` needs no Ollama installation or model. CLI and MCP integration tests start a controlled mock HTTP provider on an ephemeral literal-loopback port; they verify the real public SDK and subprocess commands without installing or invoking a model. A sandbox must permit that local listener for these integration tests.


#### MCP

The stdio adapter is documented in [the MCP guide](docs/mcp.md). It implements protocol version `2025-11-25`. Preparing a recipe does not execute a Studio workflow; only an explicit writing run with a selected installed model invokes local inference.

#### MediaPipe worker packaging

For MediaPipe 1.1.0, preserve the native ES module's dynamic WASM import. Copy `vision_bundle.mjs` next to the pinned WASM assets and import that same-origin static bundle with your bundler's dynamic-import-ignore option inside the local worker. Install the worker handler before dispatching inference, or queue the first message until initialization completes. Importing the package through a bundler that rewrites its variable WASM import can fail at runtime even when the build succeeds.

The equivalent worker entry uses the reviewed SDK handler:

```js
import * as vision from '/vision-assets/vision_bundle.mjs';
import { installVisionWorker } from './src/vision-processor.mjs';
installVisionWorker(vision);
```

Serve this entry and the static dependency assets on the host's own origin. The recipe does not select their paths. Keep the upstream dependency and model licenses with any redistributed assets.

#### Compatibility and troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Canvas preview fails | Serve the repository over localhost; use a real PNG, JPEG or WebP within the documented pixel limits. |
| Browser writer is unavailable | Check secure context, WebGPU with `shader-f16`, workers and available GPU memory. No remote fallback is enabled. |
| Vision says a model is missing | Check selected-agent setup progress, or use Download after Data Saver/manual setup. Cache-only loading cannot download it. |
| MediaPipe WASM fails to load | Serve the pinned native bundle and its WASM files together on the same origin; preserve its variable imports. |
| Ollama is unavailable | Start the service outside this SDK and use a literal-loopback endpoint. `localhost` is deliberately rejected by the Node runtime. |
| A writing run fails validation | Try a shorter brief or another eligible installed model. Invalid output is reported after one bounded repair attempt. |
| CLI reports unknown arguments | Use `node scripts/run.mjs --help` and `node scripts/smoke.mjs --help`; scaffold usage is `npm run create -- my-agent --template story-seed`. |

Model quality depends on the task and device. Tests cover orchestration, contracts, resource cleanup and controlled provider responses; they are not a benchmark of every GPU or model's creative quality.

<!-- docs/host-integration.md -->

### Integrate agents into your application

A host reads a recipe, validates it, resolves a reviewed implementation and supplies the user's selected inputs. The SDK works independently of OptimAI Studio. Start with the [browser example](examples/browser) for a complete canvas input → preview → export flow, then use the [runtime guide](docs/runtimes.md) for optional writing, vision, 3D and camera engines. The [interactive example](examples/interactive/README.md) shows the same engines without the private Studio app.

A recipe is configuration for code you have already chosen to ship. It cannot install JavaScript, select a worker URL, add a new model service or grant itself account access.

#### Use the SDK from source

Clone the [public repository](https://github.com/OptimaiNetwork/optimai-creative-agents) to use its modules directly. The snippets below assume a JavaScript module at the repository root; adjust relative imports for your application's layout. The package is not currently published to npm.

##### Install the checkout as a dependency

An application can depend on a local checkout (for example a Git submodule) and import it by name, exactly as it would a published package:

```json
{ "dependencies": { "@optimai/creative-agents": "file:../optimai-creative-agents" } }
```

```js
import { AGENT_CATALOG } from '@optimai/creative-agents';
import { runCanvasLab } from '@optimai/creative-agents/canvas-lab';
```

`npm install` links the checkout, so edits show up without reinstalling. Every public subpath is listed in `package.json` `exports` (and in [`llms.txt`](llms.txt)); files without a subpath are internal and refuse to resolve. Each subpath:

- names its `.d.mts` declaration first, so TypeScript with `moduleResolution` `bundler`, `node16` or `nodenext` types it with no `paths` mapping;
- resolves for `import` and, through a `default` condition, for CommonJS `require()` on Node versions that load ES modules synchronously (20.19+, 22.12+), so CommonJS test harnesses share the one module instance;
- keeps the optional peers optional: install `three`, `@mediapipe/tasks-vision` or `@mlc-ai/web-llm` in your application at the pinned version only if you ship the engine that needs it.

A container build that runs `npm ci` before copying sources needs the checkout's `package.json` at the linked path first. Routes that serve the SDK's own files (artwork, a starter download) should check that the folder they read names itself `@optimai/creative-agents` before serving anything from it.

#### Import and export validated JSON

```js
import { validateAgentManifest, compileAgentPrompt } from './src/index.mjs';

export async function readRecipe(file) {
  if (file.size > 65_536) throw new Error('Choose a manifest no larger than 64 KiB.');
  const result = validateAgentManifest(JSON.parse(await file.text()));
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('\n'));
  return result.manifest;
}

export function serializeRecipe(candidate) {
  const result = validateAgentManifest(candidate);
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('\n'));
  return JSON.stringify(result.manifest, null, 2) + '\n';
}

export function prepareRecipe(candidate) {
  const result = validateAgentManifest(candidate);
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('\n'));
  return compileAgentPrompt(result.manifest);
}
```

Wire `readRecipe` to an explicit file picker. Show parse and validation failures in the UI, and validate again after editing settings and before execution. Save the detached `result.manifest` rather than retaining the original mutable object. `serializeRecipe` produces portable JSON for a download or host-owned storage; persistence is a host decision. Preparing a prompt performs no inference or media processing.

The static [manifest schema](schema/agent-manifest.schema.json) uses JSON Schema 2020-12. The SDK additionally checks plain-data structure, the chosen template's category and fields, string limits and privilege values. It rejects unknown properties, accessors, hidden keys, prototype-shaped data and excessive nesting in direct JavaScript calls. Recipe briefs allow up to 4,000 characters; individual runtimes can enforce a smaller limit.

Treat recipe metadata, compiled prompts and model output as untrusted plain text. Use text nodes or your framework's escaped text rendering. Do not evaluate them or render them as raw HTML.

#### Dispatch a reviewed operation

Use the source catalog's versioned `workspace` descriptor to select an adapter your application already bundles. `getAgentWorkspace(id)` returns its `kind`, reviewed `operation` and optional presentation `headline`; `AGENT_WORKSPACE_CONTRACT_VERSION` is `1.3`; the v1 recipe schema remains unchanged. Template titles, descriptions, fields and artwork remain public presentation data. Legacy `executionKind` and `runtime` exports are retained for older consumers.

##### Input policy

`getAgentInputPolicy(id)` tells a host what to ask for before it opens a workspace. It is derived from the same `workspace` descriptor, so it needs no contract bump and no recipe change:

```js
import { getAgentInputPolicy } from '@optimai/creative-agents';

const { minFiles, maxFiles, accept, maxBytes, needs, optional, onDevice } = getAgentInputPolicy('reference-blend');
// { minFiles: 2, maxFiles: 2, accept: 'image/png,image/jpeg,image/webp', maxBytes: 20971520,
//   needs: ['canvas'], optional: [], onDevice: true }
```

Use `accept` for the file input, `maxFiles > 1` for `multiple`, and `minFiles` for empty-state copy. `needs` lists browser features from `AGENT_INPUT_NEEDS` that the agent cannot run without (`webgl` for 3D and Frame Sculpture, `web-audio` for Sound Canvas, `worker`, `wasm` and `offscreen-canvas` for vision). `optional` lists features that only enhance it: a camera, face tracking or `media-recorder` export for camera agents, and `webgpu` for writing, which can also use a local Ollama runtime. `onDevice` is `false` only for guided and sketch templates, whose result comes from a host production step. The engines stay the authority: they re-check counts, types and bytes on every run, so a policy is for interface decisions, not validation.

Keep a host-owned allowlist of supported workspace versions and operations. The catalog can describe an operation, but it cannot install an adapter in a running application. A new template that reuses a supported operation can appear and open its workspace after a reviewed SDK upgrade; a new operation or custom interface needs integration and testing first.

For example, this host deliberately exposes the four original still-image processors:

```js
import { getAgentTemplate, getAgentWorkspace, validateAgentManifest } from './src/index.mjs';
import { runLocalTool } from './src/browser-runtime.mjs';

const IMAGE_OPERATIONS = new Set(['image-filter', 'image-resize', 'image-grid', 'type-overlay']);

export async function runImageRecipe(candidate, files, signal) {
  const checked = validateAgentManifest(candidate);
  if (!checked.success) throw new Error(checked.errors.join('\n'));
  const manifest = checked.manifest;
  const templateId = manifest.recipe.templateId;
  const workspace = getAgentWorkspace(templateId);
  if (workspace?.kind !== 'canvas' || !IMAGE_OPERATIONS.has(workspace.operation)) {
    throw new Error('This host does not run this recipe. Choose an installed image tool.');
  }
  const template = getAgentTemplate(templateId);
  const values = Object.fromEntries(template.fields.map(field => [field.id, field.default]));
  Object.assign(values, manifest.recipe.values);
  return runLocalTool(workspace.operation, files, values, signal);
}
```

Supply selected browser `File` objects, pass an `AbortSignal` from your Stop control and show the returned `{ blob, width, height, filename }` as a PNG preview. The engine validates actual image signatures, dimensions and resource limits. No recipe can supply a media URL or cause this processor to fetch it. Revoke object URLs your application creates when a preview is replaced or removed.

A broader host can add these reviewed runtime adapters:

| Capability | SDK entry and dispatch | Output and host requirements |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original image processing | `browser-runtime` → `runLocalTool` | PNG; selected PNG/JPEG/WebP files and bounded settings |
| Additional composition | `canvas-lab` → `canvasLabRecipeSettings`, `runCanvasLab` | PNG and the title ink, lines, placement and scrim, transition, glitch seed or print look actually drawn; normalize defaults, canonical settings and saved v1 aliases |
| Color | `color` → `pickLegibleColor`, `analyzeImageColors`, `dominantColors`, `mixColors`; `color-grade` → `gradePixels`, `resolveGrade`, `gradeColor`; `lut` → `parseCubeLut`, `applyLut`, `filmLut`, `lutColor` | OKLab/OKLCH conversions, WCAG contrast, readable ink, deterministic image palettes, a per-pixel OKLab grade and strict `.cube` LUTs; Node and browser |
| Transitions | `transition` → `composeTransition`, `resolveTransition`, `transitionProgress`, `transitionTimes`, `transitionClipTime`; `canvas-lab` → `createTransitionClip` | Wipe, iris, light-key, push and dissolve frames between two RGBA buffers with eased time and feathered edges; a Transition Lab video clip that holds each shot and draws any frame; Node and browser |
| Glitch | `glitch` → `glitchPixels`, `planGlitch`, `randomGlitchSeed`, `mulberry32` | Seeded block, colour-trail and echo glitches on an RGBA buffer, identical bytes for the same seed; Node and browser |
| Print looks | `print` → `printPixels`, `resolvePrint`, `separateDuotone`, `bayerMatrix`, `blueNoiseMatrix` | Riso duotone, halftone dots and Floyd–Steinberg, Bayer and blue-noise dithers on an RGBA buffer, identical bytes for the same settings; Node and browser |
| Typography | `typeset` → `fitTitle`, `breakLines`, `opticalSize`, `canvasMeasure`; `text-placement` → `placeTextBlock`, `chooseTitleInk`, `fitScrim`, `regionInterest` | Balanced or paragraph line breaks and optical tracking and leading for titles, against any measure function; title placement in the calmest region of a focus map and the lightest scrim that keeps an ink readable; Node and browser |
| Browser vision | `vision-runtime` → `downloadVisionModel`, `runBrowserVision` | PNG and analysis; selected-agent setup policy, reviewed local worker and WASM assets |
| Browser writing | `browser-writing-runtime` → `createBrowserAgentRuntime` | Validated written artifact; selected-agent setup policy, supported WebGPU device and local worker |
| 3D scene | `scene-3d` → `scene3DRecipeSettings`; `scene-3d-runtime` → `createScene3DStage` | Procedural/local GLB WebGL stage, PNG and scene recipe; optional reviewed Three peer |
| Camera effects/avatar | `camera-runtime`, `camera-renderer`, `camera-tracking`, `camera-worker`, `landmark-filter` | Canvas effects and original face-driven avatar; explicit permission and local verified tracking worker |
| Music visuals | `music-reactive` → `createMusicReactiveRenderer`, `beat-tracker`; `offline-analyser` → `createOfflineAnalyser` | Measured spectrum looks with an optional flash-limited beat pulse; the host owns the audio graph, playback and recording. The offline analyser reads a decoded song at any time with live `AnalyserNode` bytes, for frame-by-frame export; Node and browser |
| Video export | `video-export` → `probeVideoExport`, `exportCanvasVideo`, `encodeCanvasVideo`, `recordCanvasVideo`, `chooseRecorderType`, `readMediaForExport`, `waitMediaReady`, `rewindMedia`, `waitForExportSetup`, `videoExportFilename`, `saveBlob` | MP4 or WebM from a canvas: frame by frame through WebCodecs with the optional `mediabunny` peer, or a real-time MediaRecorder fallback with bounded input, a real rewind and cancellable setup; errors carry a stable `code` |
| Run records | `run-record` → `createRunRecord`, `digestInputs`, `parseRunRecord`, `createRunHistory`, `runRecipeValues`; `canvas-lab` → `canvasLabRecipeValues` | A stable hash per result over template, settings, seed, SDK version and an input digest; tamper-checked JSON; a de-duplicated run list; settings back to recipe values for Remix; Node and browser |
| Settings forms | `form-schema` → `getAgentFormSchema`, `listFormFields`, `getAgentFieldRoles`, `plainFormSchema` | JSON Schema 2020-12 per template with control, step, group and role hints; one source for builders, docs, MCP and host gates; Node and browser |
| Capability probe | `capabilities` → `probeCreativeCapabilities`, `detectCreativeCapabilities`, `assessAgentCapabilities`, `modelSetupEnvironment` | What this browser and device can run (WebGPU adapter, WebGL, WebCodecs, OffscreenCanvas, `ctx.filter`, camera, memory, Save-Data) and the card words for each template, without asking for any permission; browser, testable in Node |
| Accessible motion and alt text | `accessibility` → `createMotionPreference`, `reducedMotionSettings`, `getAgentMotion`, `measureFlashes`, `frameLuminance`, `createFlashLimiter`, `describeAgentOutput`, `colorName` | One reduced-motion source with an in-app override for the 3D and frame sculpture stages, each agent's reduced variant, the WCAG 2.3.1 flash limiter and a flash meter for rendered frames, and alt text for any export written from its settings; Node and browser |
| Card previews | `card-preview` → `renderAgentPreview`, `createPreviewPlayer`, `getAgentPreview` | A small deterministic looping animation per agent for gallery cards (shapes only, no text or images, nothing flashes); hover-to-play with a poster frame for reduced motion; Node, workers and the browser |
| A/B compare | `compare` → `compareOutputs`, `compareImages`, `describeComparison`, `splitView`, `stepSplit` | How two results differ (share changed, PSNR, SSIM-lite structure, OKLab colour shift, changed region, optional diff heatmap) in numbers and plain words, plus the clip and keyboard steps for a before/after slider; Node and browser |
| Progress | `progress` → `normalizeProgress`, `describeProgress`, `progressSteps`, `createProgressReporter`, `ENGINE_PROGRESS_STAGES` | One `{ stage, message, loaded, total, frame, frames, progress }` event from vision, writing, frame sampling and canvas runs, staged words for it and a stepper; Node and browser |
| Model preparation | `model-setup` → `getModelSetupPolicy`, `createModelSetupController`, `describeModelSetup`, `formatBytes` | Automatic/manual/unsupported decision, one abortable setup state machine with byte progress, and readable sizes; host supplies the reviewed load and check calls |
| Local Ollama writing | `agent-runtime` → `runCreativeAgent` | Validated written artifact; explicitly selected eligible installed model and loopback service |
| Guided production | `compileAgentPrompt` and a host handoff | Prepared direction; the destination host runs Image, Video, Story, Character or Editor production |

Vision workspace descriptors identify `person-cutout`, `pose-reference` or `face-reference`. `CANVAS_LAB_AGENTS` derives its composition map from the same catalog. Writing descriptors use the five implemented output-contract IDs; declaring an unknown writer does not implement its output validation. Sketch descriptors identify a browser drawing workspace followed by a separate Studio production step.

Recipe fields and direct engine settings can differ. Use `canvasLabRecipeSettings(templateId, manifest.recipe.values)` for compositions: it merges template defaults, preserves legacy `format`, `text`, `style` and `intensity` aliases, and gives explicit canonical settings priority. Pass the resulting settings to `runCanvasLab(settings.operation, files, settings, signal)`. The engine validates its bounded settings again. Mockup Maker keeps its original image-resize recipe fields for compatibility, while its default workspace now selects device composition. See [runtime APIs and limits](docs/runtimes.md) for exact options and requirements.

#### Normalize portable interactive recipes

`3d:scene`, `camera:effects` and `camera:avatar` (workspace contract 1.1), `music:reactive` and `frame:sculpture` (contract 1.2), and the `canvas:print` composition (contract 1.3) are source-reviewed bindings. Keep these operations on the host allowlist; an untrusted recipe cannot add another binding. Studio consumes the same public engine modules through thin adapters. Its dialog layout, account state, asset picker, credits and production services remain private host code.

```js
import { getAgentWorkspace, validateAgentManifest } from './src/index.mjs';
import { scene3DRecipeSettings } from './src/scene-3d.mjs';
import { createScene3DStage } from './src/scene-3d-runtime.mjs';
import { cameraRecipeSettings } from './src/camera-runtime.mjs';

export async function openInteractiveRecipe(candidate, mountedContainer, options) {
  const checked = validateAgentManifest(candidate);
  if (!checked.success) throw new Error(checked.errors.join('\n'));
  const { templateId, values } = checked.manifest.recipe;
  const workspace = getAgentWorkspace(templateId);
  if (workspace?.kind === '3d' && workspace.operation === 'scene') {
    const recipe = scene3DRecipeSettings(templateId, values);
    const stage = await createScene3DStage(mountedContainer, recipe.settings, options);
    stage.camera(recipe.camera);
    return stage; // Host closes it with dispose(), and owns PNG download/reference handoff.
  }
  if (workspace?.kind === 'camera' && ['effects', 'avatar'].includes(workspace.operation)) {
    return { settings: cameraRecipeSettings(templateId, values), workspace };
    // Render with the shared camera modules; requesting camera permission is another user action.
  }
  throw new Error('This host does not support this interactive workspace.');
}
```

Use `scene3DRecipeSettings` before rendering so `finish`, `view`, focal length and percent exposure change actual materials, camera and lighting. The normalizer preserves accepted legacy free-text material fields. `cameraRecipeSettings` maps recipe effect/look/intensity/mirror controls into bounded renderer settings. Do not interpret arbitrary recipe text as executable shader, model path or worker URL.

The scene engine either loads the installed optional `three@0.186.1` peer on creation or accepts trusted injected Three/addon modules. The camera avatar renderer requires a host-supplied pinned `THREE` module; its tracker requires a host-created worker, same-origin WASM path and verified model buffer. Review these code/assets together with their licenses before shipping. See [runtime ownership and exact APIs](docs/runtimes.md#interactive-3d-scenes).

#### Promote a source release into Studio

OptimAI Studio bundles a reviewed, pinned SDK commit. Public pull-request checks validate the SDK; Studio integration additionally checks its own adapters and build. Approved title, description, settings, artwork and processor changes ship with that frontend release. Compatible new source catalog templates are listed from the bundled catalog without adding a second host ID map.

Merging the public repository does not alter the live site immediately. Maintainers promote the reviewed source revision through Studio integration checks and deploy its frontend. An incompatible new operation must wait for a host adapter; it should fail the compatibility gate rather than appear as a working agent. Account, billing, project and production API changes remain separate host work and may need a backend release.

Portable JSON recipes customize existing templates. Adding an example recipe to a GitHub pull request does not automatically turn it into a built-in catalog template or featured listing. Contribute the source catalog entry, implementation or supported operation binding, original artwork, declarations, schemas and relevant tests when proposing a new built-in agent. Editorial featuring remains a separate decision.

#### Prepare only the selected model

`network: "none"` and `execution: "declarative"` describe the recipe's privileges. A trusted host can prepare fixed public model assets after the user selects an agent, or run inference against a validated literal-loopback service. `getModelSetupPolicy` recommends automatic setup on supported devices and manual setup for Data Saver, slow connections and large-model memory limits; it performs no network request itself. Model configuration stays in host code or host environment settings; it is never read from a recipe.

Show model size, device requirements, progress and browser storage behavior as preparation starts. In manual mode, offer Download; in unsupported mode, offer basic filters, procedural demos, canvas tools or guided direction. Camera permission is a separate explicit action. Stop/cancel a download when the workspace closes and keep retry deliberate. Allow users to browse other tools while preparation runs. Run writing jobs sequentially, expose progress and cancellation, and display model failures without substituting canned creative output. Vision work should report a missing subject when detection fails.

Connect cancellation and cleanup to every asynchronous operation. Release workers, decoded images, canvases, GPU sessions and temporary URLs after completion, failure or cancellation. The [runtime guide](docs/runtimes.md) explains each engine's ownership and disposal API.

#### Show staged progress with one event shape

Vision, writing, frame sampling and canvas runs all report the same event: `{ stage, message, loaded?, total?, frame?, frames?, attempt?, progress? }`. Bytes are `loaded`/`total`, counted work is `frame`/`frames`, and `progress` (0–1) is derived when an engine does not give one. Render it once for every workspace:

```js
import { describeProgress, progressSteps } from '@optimai/creative-agents/progress';
import { runCanvasLab } from '@optimai/creative-agents/canvas-lab';

const controller = new AbortController();
const show = event => {
  status.textContent = describeProgress(event);        // "Downloading 3.1 MB of 5.8 MB · 53%", "Warming up", "Frame 4 of 8"
  stepper.render(progressSteps('canvas', event));      // [{ stage, label, state: 'done' | 'current' | 'pending' }]
  bar.value = event.progress ?? 0;
};
stop.onclick = () => controller.abort();
const result = await runCanvasLab('transition', files, values, { signal: controller.signal, onProgress: show });
```

Stages come from one list (`PROGRESS_STAGES`: check, download, verify, warmup, prepare, plan, generate, validate, repair, analyze, render, frame, export, ready), and `ENGINE_PROGRESS_STAGES` gives each engine's order for a stepper. `runCanvasLab` takes `{ signal, onProgress }` as its fourth argument (a bare `AbortSignal` still works) and reports prepare → render → frame (the transition strip) → export → ready. Vision events keep their old `phase` next to `stage` (the worker's `initialize` is now `warmup`) and downloads carry bytes; writing download events carry the reviewed model size as `total`; `extractFrameSamples` keeps its `(complete, total)` arguments and adds the event as a third. `normalizeProgress` reads older shapes, so a host can pass any of them through the same renderer.

Build your own engine's progress with `createProgressReporter(onProgress, { signal })`: it sends canonical, frozen events, stops reporting once the signal aborts (a cancelled run never repaints a stale status), and ignores a listener that throws. Cancellation itself stays with the engine's `signal`; check it between steps.

#### Warn before a click with the capability probe

Probe once per page, then let each gallery card say what will happen before anyone opens it:

```js
import { assessAgentCapabilities, probeCreativeCapabilities } from '@optimai/creative-agents/capabilities';

const report = await probeCreativeCapabilities({ timeoutMs: 1500 });
const { status, message } = assessAgentCapabilities('model-turntable', report);
// status: 'ready' | 'limited' | 'slow' | 'unsupported'
// message: '' | 'No camera found here. Try it with a photo.' | 'Runs slower on this device.' | 'Needs WebGL, which this browser doesn’t offer.'
```

`detectCreativeCapabilities()` is the synchronous half: feature presence for every `AGENT_INPUT_NEEDS` entry plus `canvas-filter` and `webcodecs`, and device hints (`memoryGB`, `cores`, `saveData`, `effectiveType`, `reducedMotion`, `coarsePointer`). `probeCreativeCapabilities` adds the two answers that need a promise: whether a WebGPU adapter exists (a software adapter sets `gpu.fallback`) and whether any camera is attached. It never calls `getUserMedia` or asks for a permission, releases its WebGL test context at once, and keeps the synchronous answer for a step that times out or is aborted.

`assessAgentCapabilities(id, report)` reads the template's input policy: a missing hard need is `unsupported`; a small device (under 4 GB or two cores), a software GPU or Data Saver before a model download is `slow` for vision, 3D, camera, frame and browser writing; a missing optional feature (camera, recording, face tracking, WebGPU for writing) is `limited` with a line that says what still works. With no report every template reads `ready`, so server rendering shows no warnings. Pass the same report to `getModelSetupPolicy(model, modelSetupEnvironment(report))` to keep one source of device facts. The engines still check on every run; a report is for interface decisions.

#### Respect reduced motion and describe every export

Every agent that moves on its own has a calm variant, and every export can carry alt text written from the settings that made it:

```js
import { createMotionPreference, describeAgentOutput, getAgentMotion, measureFlashes, frameLuminance, reducedMotionSettings } from '@optimai/creative-agents/accessibility';

const motion = createMotionPreference();            // follows the device…
motion.set('reduce');                                // …or an in-app toggle: 'system' | 'reduce' | 'full'
const stage = await createScene3DStage(container, settings, { motion }); // also createFrameSculptureStage
getAgentMotion('model-turntable').note;              // 'Turntable rotation pauses for reduced motion; you can still orbit by hand.'
if (motion.matches) settings = reducedMotionSettings('model-turntable', settings); // rotating: false

img.alt = describeAgentOutput('print-shop', values, { width: 1080, height: 1350 });
// 'Print Shop image, 1080 × 1350: print look halftone dots, riso inks pink + blue, ink color dark blue, …'
```

`createMotionPreference` is a `MediaQueryList` look-alike (`matches`, `change` events) over `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, so a stage that already listened to the device query accepts it unchanged; without a `motion` option the stages keep reading the device. `reducedMotionSettings(id, settings)` returns the reduced variant without adding keys a strict validator rejects: turntables and frame sculptures stop rotating, Sound Canvas gets `reducedMotion: true` (its calm cover, no beat pulse), and camera stages hold their animated effects. Still agents come back unchanged.

`createFlashLimiter` is the same WCAG 2.3.1 limiter the beat tracker uses (at most three evenly spaced flashes a second; the cap cannot be raised). To check rendered output, take `frameLuminance(imageData.data)` per frame and pass the series to `measureFlashes(series, { fps })`: it counts pairs of opposing changes of at least 0.1 relative luminance where the darker state is below 0.8, and reports the worst one-second window and `safe`. It measures frame averages, so it misses small-area and saturated-red flashes; treat it as a floor, not a certificate.

`describeAgentOutput(id, values, details)` writes at most 300 characters from the settings the engine actually read (`form-schema` roles), names colours in plain words (`colorName('#102031')` → `dark blue`), quotes titles, leaves seeds out and keeps the template title first. Pass what only the host knows in `details`: `width`, `height`, the drawn title `lines`, `media: 'video'`, `frames`, the 3D `subject` and `camera`, and `reducedMotion`.

#### Play a live preview on gallery cards

Every agent has a small animated preview built from the catalog, so a gallery card can show what the agent does before anyone opens it:

```js
import { createPreviewPlayer, renderAgentPreview } from '@optimai/creative-agents/card-preview';

const player = createPreviewPlayer(canvas, 'transition-lab', { motion }); // draws the poster frame now
card.addEventListener('pointerenter', () => player.play());              // false, and still the poster, under reduced motion
card.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => player.pause());             // back to the poster
card.addEventListener('focusin', () => player.play());
card.addEventListener('focusout', () => player.pause());

renderAgentPreview('poster-lab', offscreenCtx, 1200, { width: 240, height: 135 }); // one frame, anywhere
```

`renderAgentPreview(agent, ctx, t, { width, height, reducedMotion })` draws in a 480×270 space scaled to your size. A frame depends only on the agent and `t`: the loop repeats every `PREVIEW_LOOP_MS` (4.8 s), `t = 0` is a composed poster frame, and `reducedMotion` always draws it. Previews use shapes and gradients only, with no text, fonts or images, so they look the same in every browser, worker and test. Every shape keeps its colour for the whole loop and only geometry moves (a few layers fade in slowly), so nothing flashes.

`getAgentPreview(agent)` names the motif (`grade` wipes a finished look across a picture, `iris` opens a transition, `bars` is Sound Canvas, `strip` is a guided workflow's filmstrip…) and an OKLab palette from the catalog accent; music, frame, 3D and camera agents get a dark stage. Pass a template-like object (`{ id, accent, workspace: { kind, operation } }`) to preview a community agent from its manifest; unknown IDs get the filmstrip. `createPreviewPlayer` sizes the canvas to its CSS box at up to 2× density, caps playback at 30 frames a second, and stops at once when a `motion` preference (a boolean, `createMotionPreference()` or a `MediaQueryList`) turns on reduced motion.

#### Compare two results with a before/after slider

Show what a finish, a new seed or a different run actually changed, side by side on one artboard:

```js
import { compareImages, describeComparison, splitView, stepSplit } from '@optimai/creative-agents/compare';

const result = await compareImages(earlierBlob, latestBlob, { signal });   // Blobs, blob: URLs, bitmaps or ImageData
note.textContent = describeComparison(result);   // "Small changes to 4% of the image · structure 93% kept"
const view = splitView(slider.value / 100);       // the earlier layer sits over the latest one
earlierImage.style.clipPath = view.clipPath;      // "inset(0 50% 0 0)"
divider.style.left = `${view.position * 100}%`;
handle.addEventListener('keydown', event => { const next = stepSplit(position, event.key); if (next !== undefined) setPosition(next); });
```

`compareOutputs(a, b, options)` measures two RGBA buffers (`ImageData` or `{ data, width, height }`) on one grid: `a`'s aspect, no larger than either image, and at most `maxSide` (512 by default) on the long side, so a 4K export costs the same as a thumbnail. Pixels are box-averaged onto the grid and transparent ones are read over mid grey. It returns `changed` (the share of pixels whose largest channel moved more than `threshold`, 8 by default), `meanDelta` and `maxDelta` (0–1), `psnr` in dB (`Infinity` when identical), `ssim` (SSIM-lite: the mean SSIM of half-overlapping 8 × 8 windows on luma; 1 is the same structure), `deltaE` (the mean OKLab distance), `overall` (the same colour shift and structure on a grid of at most 24 pixels, where grain, dither and halftone dots average out), `bounds` (the changed region in `a`'s pixels) and, with `{ diff: true }`, an RGBA heatmap of the change. The same two buffers always give the same numbers, and the metrics are symmetric when the sizes match. Different sizes still compare (`sameSize: false`); `b` is stretched to `a`'s aspect.

`compareImages` is the browser path: it decodes each source once straight onto the comparison grid, reports `width`, `height` and `bounds` in `a`'s full pixels, closes the bitmaps it opened and stops when `signal` aborts. `describeComparison` says *Identical*, *No visible change* (only sub-threshold noise), *Small changes to …*, *Same picture with new grain or texture across …* (pixels differ but the overall look moved less than about one just-noticeable OKLab step, as when only a Print Shop or Glitch Cut seed changed), *Changed …* or *A new look across …*, with the share of the image and how much structure was kept. `splitView(position, width, height, { orientation })` gives the visible before and after rectangles, the divider line and the CSS `clipPath`; `stepSplit` moves a custom handle by 5% per arrow key, 20% per Page key, and to the ends on Home and End. A native range input needs neither.

#### Export video with WebCodecs or the recorder

Ask once which path this browser can take, then encode frame by frame or record in real time:

```js
import { probeVideoExport, exportCanvasVideo, exportFrameCount, videoExportFilename, saveBlob } from '@optimai/creative-agents/video-export';

const mediabunny = await import('mediabunny').catch(() => null);        // optional peer, pinned 1.62.1
const probe = await probeVideoExport({ width: 1280, height: 720, fps: 30, audio: true, mediabunny });
const video = await exportCanvasVideo({
  probe, mediabunny, canvas, fps: 30, frames: exportFrameCount(song.duration, 30), audio: decodedSong,   // an AudioBuffer
  render: (frame, seconds) => drawFrameAt(seconds), signal, onProgress: event => showProgress(event),
});
saveBlob(video.blob, videoExportFilename(title, video.mime, { suffix: '· visualizer' }));   // video.engine: 'webcodecs' | 'recorder'
```

`probeVideoExport` resolves to `{ engine, container, mime, extension, videoCodec, audioCodec, recorderType, reason }`. With WebCodecs and the peer it tries MP4 (H.264, then VP9, AV1, HEVC; AAC, then Opus) before WebM (VP9, VP8, AV1; Opus), using the peer's `canEncodeVideo`/`canEncodeAudio` or the browser's `isConfigSupported`. `recorderType` is always the best MediaRecorder type, so a host can fall back without probing again; `reason` says why WebCodecs was skipped (`webcodecs-missing`, `muxer-missing` or `codec-missing`). Sides must be even and at most 4096 pixels.

`encodeCanvasVideo` calls `render(frame, seconds)` for each frame, adds it with an exact timestamp and reports the shared progress shape (`prepare`, `frame` N of M, `export`, `ready`). Because it does not depend on playback, it runs faster than real time where the encoder allows, keeps working in a background tab and never drops a frame. Cancelling, a render error or an encoder error cancels the output, so a partial file is never returned; a file over `maxBytes` (128 MiB by default) is refused.

`exportCanvasVideo` takes the probe and runs the path it chose with the same `render(frame, seconds)` contract, so a host writes one export. On the recorder path it calls `recordCanvasVideo`: the canvas is captured with `captureStream(0)`, each frame is drawn, pushed with `requestFrame()` (or captured at the frame rate where a track lacks it) and held for 1/fps of wall-clock time while MediaRecorder writes it; frame 0 is drawn before recording starts. An `AudioBuffer` plays into the recording from frame 0 through a Web Audio graph that is never routed to the speakers (`audioTracks` adds live tracks instead). The tab must stay visible, since hidden tabs slow timers. If WebCodecs fails mid-way (`encoder-failed`) and the probe named a recorder type, the export restarts once on the recorder; pass `fallback: false` to surface the error instead. The result's `engine` says which path made the file, and `unsupported`, `recorder-missing`, `recorder-failed` and `audio-missing` join the error codes.

To render a song frame by frame, decode it once (`await audioContext.decodeAudioData(bytes)`) and read it with `createOfflineAnalyser` from `@optimai/creative-agents/offline-analyser`. `analyser.getByteFrequencyData(bytes, seconds)` gives the bytes a live `AnalyserNode` with the same `fftSize`, `smoothingTimeConstant`, `minDecibels` and `maxDecibels` would show at that moment (mono down-mix, Blackman window, smoothing over successive reads), so the existing music-reactive and beat-tracker code draws the same picture as playback. Read times in order and call `reset()` before another export. For Sound Canvas looks, `createMusicReactiveRenderer` from `music-reactive` wraps the analyser, beat tracker and smoothing into `draw(ctx, frame)`; see [music and motion](docs/MUSIC-MOTION.md).

Transition Lab has a ready clip: `createTransitionClip(files, values, { width, seconds, hold })` from `canvas-lab` opens both shots with the same smart crop and style as a run and returns `{ canvas, width, height, seconds, style, draw(frame, frames), close() }`. Each shot holds still for `hold` (15%) of the clip at both ends, and the move between them eases with the recipe pace (`transitionClipTime` gives the raw time). Pass `render: frame => clip.draw(frame, frames)` to `exportCanvasVideo` and `close()` the clip afterwards. The [playground](examples/playground/README.md) has an **Export video** button built this way. Frame Sculpture's `stage.turntable()` returns the same shape for an orbit of the framed view ([music and motion](docs/MUSIC-MOTION.md#frame-sculpture-frame-sculpture)).

For the real-time path, `chooseRecorderType` picks a MediaRecorder type, `readMediaForExport` buffers a whole source with a byte cap (64 MiB by default), `waitMediaReady` and `rewindMedia` wait for real `canplay` and `seeked` events, and `waitForExportSetup` wraps a `resume()` or `play()` promise that may never settle with a cancel and a timeout. `checkExportDuration` returns `null`, `'unreadable'` or `'too-long'` (over five minutes by default). Every failure is a `VideoExportError` with a stable `code` (`source-too-large`, `seek-timeout`, `setup-timeout`, `encoder-failed`…) and a plain English default `message`, so a host can show its own words. Each wait helper takes injectable `timers` for tests.

#### Render settings from the form schema

Build settings forms, docs tables and host checks from one schema instead of copying field IDs and choices:

```js
import { getAgentFormSchema, listFormFields } from '@optimai/creative-agents/form-schema';

const schema = getAgentFormSchema('poster-lab');      // JSON Schema 2020-12 for recipe `values`
for (const group of schema['x-ui'].groups) {          // content, look, color, layout, motion (non-empty, in order)
  renderHeading(group.title);
  for (const field of listFormFields(schema).filter(entry => entry.group === group.id)) renderControl(field);
}
```

Each property has the same bounds `validateRecipeValues` enforces (`enum`, `minimum`/`maximum`, `maxLength`, the hex `pattern` for colors), a `title`, a `default` and an `x-ui` object:

| Hint | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `control` | `text`, `textarea`, `select`, `color` (hex settings), `slider`, `stepper` (ranges of 12 or less), `number` (wide ranges such as pixel sizes), `seed` (offer a reroll) |
| `step` | Number controls only; `1` for whole-number settings |
| `group`, `order` | Where the setting goes; `x-ui.order` lists every setting in display order, aliases after the setting they stand in for |
| `role` | `engine` (the on-device workspace reads it), `alias` (an older recipe name used only when `aliasOf` is missing, such as Poster Lab's `format` for `ratio`), `brief` (shapes the prepared brief only), `unused` (reaches neither; only possible for unreviewed templates) |

Alias and brief settings in on-device workspaces carry a `description` that says so, which a builder can show as a hint. `getAgentFormSchema` also accepts a template object, so a host can check a candidate before promoting it: refuse `unused` roles and controls it cannot draw, and run every `engine` choice and endpoint through the engine's normalizer. `plainFormSchema` drops the `x-` hints for strict validators; the [MCP adapter](docs/mcp.md) builds each tool's `values` schema from it. Schemas are fresh plain JSON on every call and describe saved recipe values only; engine-only settings (for example a canvas title's `ink`) stay outside v1 recipes.

#### Read form controls and share playground links

`@optimai/creative-agents/playground` holds the small rules every settings form needs, so a host draws controls and the SDK decides what a value means. The [Agent Playground](examples/playground/README.md) is built from these alone:

```js
import { formDefaults, readFormValue, colorInputValue, rerollSeed, playgroundRunPlan, encodePlaygroundState, decodePlaygroundState, listPlaygroundAgents } from '@optimai/creative-agents/playground';

const schema = getAgentFormSchema('glitch-cut'), fields = listFormFields(schema);
let values = formDefaults(schema);                                  // { effect: 'block displacement', amount: 35, seed: 1, … }
values.amount = readFormValue(fields.find(f => f.id === 'amount'), input.value); // '' → default, '500' → 100, '41.6' → 42
values.seed = rerollSeed(fields.find(f => f.id === 'seed'), values.seed);        // always a new look within bounds
const plan = playgroundRunPlan('glitch-cut', values);               // { runner: 'canvas-lab', operation: 'glitch', settings }
location.hash = encodePlaygroundState({ agent: 'glitch-cut', values }); // agent=glitch-cut&seed=48213
```

`readFormValue(field, raw)` turns what a control holds into a value the recipe validator accepts: numbers are parsed, rounded and clamped, and an empty or unreadable number falls back to the default instead of becoming `0`; a choice outside the list and a malformed hex fall back; text is cut to its limit. Pass `{ partial: true }` on each keystroke of a hex text box so `#3a` survives while someone types, and read it again without it when the field loses focus. Number boxes read best the same way: keep typing free and snap on `change`. `colorInputValue` gives an `<input type="color">` the `#rrggbb` it insists on (`#abc` expands).

`listPlaygroundAgents()` lists every agent a form alone can run (canvas and vision), with its `runner` (`canvas-lab`, `local-tool` or `vision`), its file `inputs` from the input policy and, for vision, the pinned model to set up first. `playgroundRunPlan(id, values)` validates the values and returns the call to make: engine settings for `runCanvasLab` (v1 aliases mapped), the defaults plus values for `runLocalTool`, or `normalizeVisionValues` options and the model for `runBrowserVision`.

`encodePlaygroundState` writes a short query string with the agent and only the settings that differ from its defaults; it refuses values a recipe would refuse and links over 4096 characters. `decodePlaygroundState` reads a hash or query as untrusted text: unknown agents give `null`, and each setting is kept only when it reads back exactly, so a clamped number, an unknown key or a choice from another agent is listed in `dropped` and left at its default instead of being changed silently. Images never go in a link.

#### List the starter kits

`@optimai/creative-agents/starter-kits` is the catalog behind `npm run create -- --kit`. It reads no files, so a host can show the kits, or build a kit folder itself, without Node.js:

```js
import { listStarterKits, starterKitCommand, planStarterKit, starterKitVariables, fillStarterFile } from '@optimai/creative-agents/starter-kits';

for (const kit of listStarterKits()) console.log(kit.title, kit.runtime, starterKitCommand(kit)); // npm run create -- --kit poster-app
const plan = planStarterKit('poster-app', { name: 'my-poster' });             // { folder: 'my-poster', files: [{ path, template: 'kits/poster-app/…' }] }
const variables = starterKitVariables('poster-app', { name: 'my-poster', sdkPath: '../..' });
const html = fillStarterFile(templateText, variables);                       // fills {{NAME}}, {{TITLE}}, {{SDK_PATH}}, {{IMPORT_MAP}}…
```

Each kit names the catalog `agents` it is built on and the public `subpaths` it imports; `starterKitImportMap(kit, sdkPath)` maps exactly those subpaths for a page with no bundler. `sdkPath` must be a relative folder (forward slashes, no scheme or root), names must be lowercase and hyphenated, and an unknown or unfilled `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` throws, so a kit is never written half-filled.

#### Keep run records and remix exact settings

Give every result a run record, so a creator can return to it, compare it and remix it with the exact settings that drew it:

```js
import { createRunHistory, createRunRecord, digestInputs } from '@optimai/creative-agents/run-record';
import { canvasLabRecipeValues } from '@optimai/creative-agents/canvas-lab';

const history = createRunHistory({ limit: 8, settleMs: 1500 });
const inputsDigest = await digestInputs(files);            // bytes only, in order; names never count
const record = createRunRecord({ templateId: 'glitch-cut', settings, sdkVersion: '0.5.0', inputsDigest, output: { width, height } });
const { evicted } = history.add(record, URL.createObjectURL(blob));
for (const entry of evicted) URL.revokeObjectURL(entry.attachment);
const { values, extra } = canvasLabRecipeValues(record.templateId, record.settings);   // Remix: v1 recipe values
```

`record.hash` is 16 hex characters over the template, the settings as canonical JSON, the seed (taken from `settings.seed` when present), the SDK version and the input digest, so the same run gets the same hash in every browser and any change gets a new one; `createdAt` and `output` are carried but not hashed. `digestInputs` uses SHA-256 from Web Crypto and falls back to a 64-bit hash (`h64:`) where Web Crypto is missing. `parseRunRecord` reads shared JSON and throws when its contents no longer match its hash; `verifyRunRecord` returns a boolean.

`createRunHistory` keeps runs newest first and never twice: adding a hash it already has moves that run to the front. With `settleMs`, a run made within that time of the previous one replaces it, so a slider drag leaves one entry; `settle()` keeps the newest run (call it on export). Release each `evicted` attachment.

For Remix, `canvasLabRecipeValues` turns canvas engine settings back into the template's v1 recipe values (engine names such as `push` become recipe names such as *camera move*) and returns the engine-only settings that differ from the defaults as `extra`; `runRecipeValues` does the same split for any template without aliases. A run record is not a manifest: keep sharing recipes as manifests, and treat records as provenance next to the result.

#### Design around the actual result

Use one clear primary action for each step: choose input, run, review and export. Name the output accurately, for example **Export PNG**, **Write storyboard**, or **Continue in Story Studio**. A still-image transition preview is a PNG, and a prepared video brief is direction for an editor.

Preserve user inputs after a failure and explain the next recovery step. Support labeled controls, keyboard use, visible focus, readable text, reduced motion and small screens. Verify export, retry, cancellation and no-subject flows in a real browser in addition to controlled tests.

Canvas and model runtimes do not need a Studio account. If your application hands off paid production or publishing, display the selected references, destination, preview and applicable cost before that action. Account access, billing, project persistence and publishing belong to the host; an agent's prose cannot authorize them.

#### Extend the contract deliberately

| Change | Required work |
| --- | --- |
| Remix a reviewed recipe | Keep a known template ID, approved values and v1 capability fields; validate and share JSON |
| Add a new operation or model | Contribute implementation, declarations, contract changes, tests and documentation; release and integrate reviewed source |
| Add MCP client support | Configure the local [stdio adapter](docs/mcp.md); authorize prepared direction and explicit writing runs in the client |
| Offer agents from your own MCP server or list them in your docs | `mcp-tools` → `mcpToolDefinitions`, `prepareMcpRecipe`, `mcpRecipeExports`: the adapter's own definitions with output schemas, icons and a stable order ([guide](docs/mcp.md#build-your-own-mcp-tools)) |

Keep stable agent IDs and increment a recipe's `version` when releasing a revision. A breaking manifest format needs a new `schemaVersion` and a deliberate migration. Legacy Tool-named exports and manifests remain aliases of the v1 Agent contract, so saved recipes can reopen.

Unknown template IDs are rejected. JSON import cannot install a new capability; new source requires maintainer review and a host that bundles it. Follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#new-reviewed-operations) for source changes, including generated schemas, model/dependency licenses and hardware requirements.

The `music/reactive` and `frame/sculpture` adapters are installed with workspace contract 1.2. Contract 1.3 adds the `print` canvas operation (Print Shop); a host that bundles `canvas-lab` runs it through `runCanvasLab` like the other compositions. See [music and motion engines](docs/MUSIC-MOTION.md) for their host lifecycle and export contracts.

<!-- docs/CAMERA.md -->

### Reusable camera and avatar agents

`camera-stage` and `avatar-stage` share portable browser engines. The Studio supplies its dialog, authentication, camera permission buttons, capture controls and explicit media handoff. These UI responsibilities do not enter the SDK.

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `camera-runtime` | Bounded rig math, speed-adaptive rig smoothing, face-loss reset, safe recipe settings and camera leases |
| `landmark-filter` | One-Euro scalar and vector filters for face and pose landmarks |
| `camera-tracking` | One frame in flight, throttling, timeout/cancellation and worker lifecycle |
| `camera-worker` | Checksum verification and MediaPipe VIDEO inference in a host worker |
| `camera-renderer` | Canvas effects, face-anchored halo and original procedural avatars |
| `vision-runtime` | Shared cache-first, checksum-verified model download and owned model buffers |

The host pins its MediaPipe executable module and WASM files on its own origin. `installCameraWorker(vision)` receives that imported module. `createFaceTracker(buffer, { workerFactory, wasmBaseUrl, onFace, onError, signal })` receives a host worker factory and a same-origin WASM path; it never downloads executable code. Its initialized task uses VIDEO mode, one face, blendshapes and transformation matrices. The worker checks the fixed face-model checksum again before task creation.

```js
import { loadVisionModelBuffer } from '@optimai/creative-agents/vision-runtime';
import { createFaceTracker } from '@optimai/creative-agents/camera-tracking';

const modelBuffer = await loadVisionModelBuffer('face-reference', {
  signal,
  onProgress,
  downloadIfMissing: true,
});
const tracker = await createFaceTracker(modelBuffer, {
  signal,
  workerFactory: () => new Worker(new URL('./camera.worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' }),
  wasmBaseUrl: '/vendor/mediapipe/1.1.0',
  onFace,
  onError,
});
tracker.submit(unmirroredFrameCanvas, performance.now());
// On close, account change or hidden document:
tracker.dispose();
```

`loadVisionModelBuffer` returns an owned copy. It reuses the same verified memory/Cache API weights as still-image vision agents. `downloadIfMissing: false` is strictly cache-only. Automatic setup should be visible, cancellable, cache-first and defer network on data-saving or slow connections. Camera permission must remain a separate user action. The face model is about 3.6 MB; the pinned local runtime/WASM is loaded separately during worker initialization.

For 3D rendering, inject a host's pinned Three module:

```js
import { createCameraAvatar } from '@optimai/creative-agents/camera-renderer';

const avatar = createCameraAvatar(canvas, 'orbit', { THREE });
const smoother = createFaceRigSmoother(); // one per preview loop
avatar.render(smoother.next(faceRigAt(frame, now, mirror), now));
avatar.dispose();
```

Avatars are original procedural characters. They animate geometry from bounded face coefficients and use no likeness texture. Matrix packing is column-major, matching MediaPipe's serialized MatrixData. Mirroring is applied to the visible output and rig, after unmirrored inference, so left/right face coefficients remain consistent. A missing live face releases the rig toward neutral after 500 ms. The One-Euro rig smoother keeps the avatar still while the head rests and lets turns and blinks through without the lag of a fixed moving average; see [landmark smoothing](docs/runtimes.md#landmark-smoothing).

Camera and portrait pixels remain local. Model requests contact only the fixed official weight URL, with credentials omitted and no referrer. Cache and network responses are size-bounded before SHA-256 validation. Hosts retain ownership of consent, local exports and any later cloud Studio handoff.

<!-- docs/MUSIC-MOTION.md -->

### Music and motion engines

Two browser engines extend the catalog in SDK 0.4.0 / workspace contract 1.2, and run unchanged on workspace contract 1.3. They use selected local media, have no cloud provider, and require no model download. The portable v1 manifest still carries only a declarative recipe. An application must install the matching reviewed adapter before it can run these workspaces.

#### Sound Canvas (`music-reactive`)

The `music/reactive` workspace draws four original looks: Orbital bloom, Silk ribbons, Spectrum stage and Midnight aurora. The engine is dependency-free, deterministic and bounded. Its input is playback time and actual analyser data. Normalized frequency bytes are display signals, **not** loudness, BPM, beat timestamps or a music transcription. For tempo and beats, add the separate beat tracker below.

```js
import {
  extractMusicReactiveFeatures,
  smoothMusicReactiveFeatures,
  renderMusicReactiveFrame,
} from '@optimai/creative-agents/music-reactive';

analyser.fftSize = 2048;
analyser.smoothingTimeConstant = 0;
const bytes = new Uint8Array(analyser.frequencyBinCount);
analyser.getByteFrequencyData(bytes);
const measured = extractMusicReactiveFeatures(bytes, {
  sampleRate: audioContext.sampleRate, fftSize: analyser.fftSize,
});
// Retain the prior result between frames. Reset it to null after a seek/source change.
const features = smoothMusicReactiveFeatures(previousFeatures, measured, elapsedMs);
renderMusicReactiveFrame(canvas.getContext('2d'), {
  width: canvas.width, height: canvas.height, time: audio.currentTime,
  look: 'orbital', intensity: 0.7, title: 'Your song', ...features,
  reducedMotion: matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches,
});
```

The host owns the audio graph, file selection, playback, canvas, recording and disposal. Use one `MediaElementAudioSourceNode` per media element and route it to an analyser, speakers and a `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode`. Full-song recording can combine `canvas.captureStream()` with a **clone** of the destination audio track. Stop cloned export tracks without destroying the reusable audio graph. Check `MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported()`, handle runtime encoder failures, wait for a real seek to the beginning, bound retained chunks, and discard a canceled or hidden-tab recording instead of presenting it as complete. If recording APIs are absent, provide preview and still export. The [`video-export`](docs/host-integration.md#export-video-with-webcodecs-or-the-recorder) module provides these recorder helpers (`chooseRecorderType`, `readMediaForExport`, `waitMediaReady`, `rewindMedia`, `waitForExportSetup`) and, with the optional `mediabunny` peer, a frame-by-frame WebCodecs path that does not depend on playback. For that path, decode the song to an `AudioBuffer` and read it with `createOfflineAnalyser` (`offline-analyser` subpath): it returns the same bytes a live analyser would show at each frame's time, so the export looks like playback, runs faster than real time and keeps going in a hidden tab. Pass `smoothingTimeConstant: 0` there too when the elapsed-time smoother runs after it.

`createMusicReactiveRenderer(song, { fps, look, intensity, title, artist, reducedMotion, beatSync })` does all of that in one object: `renderer.draw(ctx, frame)` reads the song at `frame / fps`, extracts features, runs the same flash-limited beat tracker and elapsed-time smoothing as playback, and draws the frame (width and height default to the canvas). `renderer.frames` covers the song. Draw frames in order; an earlier frame starts the smoothing again, so an export that restarts stays correct. Pass it as `render: frame => renderer.draw(ctx, frame)` with `audio: song` to `exportCanvasVideo`.

##### Beat sync (`beat-tracker`)

`beat-tracker` reads the same analyser bytes and finds onsets, tempo and beats on the device. It has no dependencies, no timers and no model, and it runs in Node for tests.

1. **Onsets.** Spectral flux on 24 logarithmic bands (30 Hz–11 kHz) counts how much each band rose since the last frame. An onset is a rising crossing of an adaptive threshold: `0.012 + sensitivity × median(flux over the last second)`.
2. **Tempo.** Every pair of recent onsets (eight seconds, at most 64) votes for the tempo of its interval and of its halves, thirds and quarters. This is the autocorrelation of the onset train on a log-tempo axis. A mild prior around 120 BPM breaks ties, and a doubled tempo that the onsets support almost as well wins, so off-beat hi-hats do not halve the count. Confidence measures how tightly the onsets sit on the chosen grid, above what chance would give.
3. **Beat clock.** A second-order phase-locked loop predicts each beat from the tempo and pulls its phase and period toward onsets that land near a prediction. It keeps time through a fill and drops the lock after four seconds without onsets.

```js
import { createBeatTracker, prefersReducedMotion } from '@optimai/creative-agents/beat-tracker';

const beats = createBeatTracker({
  sampleRate: audioContext.sampleRate, fftSize: analyser.fftSize,
  reducedMotion: prefersReducedMotion(),
});
// Every animation frame, after analyser.getByteFrequencyData(bytes):
const beat = beats.push(bytes, audio.currentTime * 1000);
renderMusicReactiveFrame(ctx, { ...frameOptions, ...features, pulse: beat.pulse });
// beat.onset, beat.bpm, beat.confidence, beat.locked, beat.beat, beat.phase (0 → 1)
```

Pass the **playback** time, not the wall clock, so beats follow pauses and seeks. A backwards step or a jump of more than a second resets the tracker. On tracked synthetic material, predicted beats land within about one frame of the true beat: under 25 ms at 60 fps and under 45 ms at 30 fps. At 30 fps, tempos above about 160 BPM can lock to half time. That is still on the beat, and the flash cap would thin those pulses anyway.

**Photosensitivity.** `pulse` is a 0–1 envelope that starts only on a *flash-limited* beat. `createFlashLimiter()` allows at most three flashes in any one second, evenly spaced, as [WCAG 2.3.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold) requires, and the cap cannot be raised. Sound Canvas uses the pulse to swell geometry only. It never changes colour or brightness. With reduced motion, the tracker still reports tempo and beats, but `flash` is always false and `pulse` is 0. The renderer also ignores `pulse` when `reducedMotion` is set. The limiter is shared: `accessibility` exports the same `createFlashLimiter`, plus `measureFlashes` and `frameLuminance` to check a rendered visualizer, `reducedMotionSettings('music-reactive', settings)` for the calm variant and `describeAgentOutput('music-reactive', settings, { media: 'video' })` for its alt text. See [reduced motion and alt text](docs/host-integration.md#respect-reduced-motion-and-describe-every-export).

`estimateTempo(onsetTimesMs)`, `logBandSpectrum` and `spectralFlux` expose the pure steps. To check that an edit cuts on the beat, pass the tracker's beat times to `checkCutAlignment` in `verify`.

#### Frame Sculpture (`frame-sculpture`)

The `frame/sculpture` workspace extracts up to twelve actual frames from selected video and arranges them as textured planes. It is explicitly a **2.5D composition, not 3D reconstruction**. Local MP4/WebM/MOV/M4V clips are decoded using the browser's installed codecs; PNG/JPEG/WebP stills become one plane. Animated GIF extraction is unsupported. Source files are limited to 64 MB and video to 60 seconds; textures are reduced to a 768-pixel edge.

```js
import { extractFrameSamples, createFrameSculptureStage } from '@optimai/creative-agents/frame-sculpture';
import { describeProgress } from '@optimai/creative-agents/progress';
const abort = new AbortController();
const result = await extractFrameSamples(selectedFile, {
  count: 8, signal: abort.signal, onProgress: (done, total, event) => showProgress(describeProgress(event)), // "Frame 4 of 8"
});
const stage = await createFrameSculptureStage(container, {
  layout: 'fan', spacing: 0.26, spread: 0.8,
}, { onError: showError });
stage.frames(result.frames); // Takes ownership after validating the complete frame set.
const png = await stage.png();
const recipe = stage.configuration(); // Settings, sample times and camera; no source file bytes.
stage.dispose(); // Releases renderer, textures, retained canvases, observers and listeners.
```

For a video of the composition, `stage.turntable()` orbits the view the creator framed around its target and returns `{ canvas, width, height, degrees, draw(frame, frames), close() }`. The canvas has even video sides from the stage's aspect (longer side `edge`, 1280 by default) or explicit `width`/`height`; `degrees` (360 by default, negative to turn the other way) is the orbit per clip, and a full orbit never repeats its first frame, so the clip loops. While it is open, the stage stops its auto-orbit and ignores resizes; `close()` puts the camera, size and motion back. `FRAME_SCULPTURE_TURNTABLE` holds the default clip (6 s at 30 fps), `turntableAngle` and `turntableSize` the maths:

```js
import { exportCanvasVideo, exportFrameCount, probeVideoExport } from '@optimai/creative-agents/video-export';
const spin = stage.turntable(), frames = exportFrameCount(6, 30);
try {
  const probe = await probeVideoExport({ width: spin.width, height: spin.height, fps: 30, audio: false, mediabunny });
  const video = await exportCanvasVideo({ probe, mediabunny, canvas: spin.canvas, frames, fps: 30, render: frame => spin.draw(frame, frames) });
} finally { spin.close(); }
```

Three.js is an optional pinned peer. Hosts may supply their reviewed `THREE` and `OrbitControls` through `createFrameSculptureStageWithRuntime()`; this avoids duplicate engines. If transferring the frame set fails, the caller must invoke `releaseFrameSamples()`. The renderer respects reduced motion, hidden tabs and off-screen visibility. Keep original source media alongside exported configurations; the JSON is a composition record, not an embedded media archive.

<!-- docs/mcp.md -->

### Connect the local MCP adapter

The optional adapter exposes all 39 reviewed templates to an MCP client over local stdio. Calls prepare recipes by default. Five writing templates can also run an explicitly selected model already installed in a local Ollama service. Browser canvas, vision, 3D and camera execution use the browser SDK in a host application.

The adapter implements the fixed protocol version **2025-11-25**. It does not provide a remote endpoint or install arbitrary community servers in OptimAI Studio.

#### Configure your client

Clone the [public repository](https://github.com/OptimaiNetwork/optimai-creative-agents) as described in the [quickstart](docs/quickstart.md). Use Node.js 20 or newer and the actual absolute path to your checkout:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "optimai-creative-agents": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/optimai-creative-agents/src/mcp-server.mjs"]
    }
  }
}
```

This is a common `mcpServers` configuration shape; use your client's documented equivalent if its format differs. Launch Node directly because npm's banners can corrupt JSON-RPC stdout. The adapter needs no dependency installation, API key, Studio account or model to list tools and prepare recipes.

The client sends `initialize`, checks the returned protocol version, sends `notifications/initialized`, then uses `tools/list` or `tools/call`. Stable tool names are `optimai.<template-id>`. Each tool's `values` schema comes from the SDK's [form schema](docs/host-integration.md#render-settings-from-the-form-schema), so bounds, hex patterns and alias notes match what a host builder renders. The adapter also supports `ping` and cancellation of an active local writing run.

#### Try a preparation call without a client

Run this from the repository root to exercise the real adapter with newline-delimited requests:

```sh
node src/mcp-server.mjs <<'JSONRPC'
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"builder-check","version":"1.0.0"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"optimai.story-seed","arguments":{"values":{"form":"manga","style":"manga","audience":"all ages"},"brief":"An explorer helps a lost cloud find its way home."}}}
JSONRPC
```

You should receive two JSON responses: initialization with `protocolVersion: "2025-11-25"`, then a successful call with `structuredContent.templateId: "story-seed"`, the settings and prepared prompt. The notification has no response. No inference occurs, and the process exits when stdin closes.

In a connected client, the equivalent tool-call parameters are:

```json
{
  "name": "optimai.story-seed",
  "arguments": {
    "values": { "form": "manga", "style": "manga", "audience": "all ages" },
    "brief": "An explorer helps a lost cloud find its way home."
  }
}
```

Preparation returns validated settings, a prompt, a Studio destination and the source template's `workspace` descriptor in `structuredContent`, plus the same JSON as text for older clients. Two more content blocks follow: a `resource_link` to the agent's artwork and an embedded `resource` holding a recipe file (`<id>.agent.json`, manifest v1.0) with the call's settings and brief, which a creator can save and import into any host that reads recipes, including Studio's **Saved** library. It does not read media, generate a storybook, modify an image or publish a project. The returned `runtime` and `localOperation` remain legacy catalog metadata; use a supported workspace adapter as described in [host integration](docs/host-integration.md).

#### What a client sees

Every tool in `tools/list` carries:

- **`outputSchema`**: the JSON Schema of `structuredContent` for a successful call, with an `object` root as the specification requires. It pins `templateId`, `workspace` and the other descriptors to constants and lists every setting with the same bounds as the input. Writing tools accept either a prepared recipe or, after `execution: "run"`, a written result (`anyOf`). Error results (`isError: true`) carry text only.
